name: A few passengers
why: [0, 7, 7, 34, 34, 61, 150]. If 150 is missing, the counter list is one too short: ages go up to 150, so it needs 151 counters.

name: Empty
why: No ages: []. If this failed with an error, the code reads ages[0] or max(ages) on an empty list. A count list of 151 zeros works for any input.

name: All the same
why: Five 20s: [20, 20, 20, 20, 20]. If you got one 20, the code writes each age once instead of count[v] times.

name: Input not changed
why: Return a new list and leave the input alone. If the second list changed, the code wrote the sorted ages back into ages.

name: 1.5 million passengers
expr: (lambda out: [len(out), out == [*__import__('itertools').chain.from_iterable([v] * 9_934 for v in range(151))], out[:3], out[len(out) // 2], out[-3:]])(sort_ages(args[0]))
show: 1,500,034 ages from 0 to 150; [length, exactly right?, first three, middle, last three]
why: Counting is two short passes: O(n + 151). A comparison sort written in Python needs about 30 million steps here and runs out of time.
